intro-1.text: Picture this. You're running the Dixie Road and Mayfield Road widening. Two roads, crews out every day, the Region watching. It's Monday, seven a.m.

intro-2.text: Over the weekend, the updates piled up. Daily site reports from the field. A schedule that moved. Costs landing in finance. Extra work waiting on the client's sign-off.

intro-3.text: Every one of them matters. None of them talk to each other. And the one question you actually have, are we okay, isn't answered in any of them.

intro-4.text: So you start calling. The project manager, the superintendent, accounting. By Thursday you have an answer. By then, it's already cost you.

meet-1.text: Now imagine you just ask. TaskForce AI goes through every one of those updates for you, and comes back with one page: what's wrong, how bad, and what to do first.

meet-2.text: And every number on that page comes straight from your own records.

brief-lead.text: So let's do exactly that. Monday, seven a.m., one question.

brief-ask.text: What should I worry about on Dixie this week?

brief-wait.text: Watch it work. It's going through the schedule, the site reports, the money and the delays, all at once. The part that normally takes your team a week.

brief-point.text: And there it is. What's wrong, how bad, and what to do first: your whole Monday meeting, before your coffee. The tiles show where the job stands against the plan.

brief-verify.text: Look at what's waiting on the Region's sign-off. And the map: Dixie Road and Mayfield Road, exactly where the work is.

send-lead.text: Talha runs Dixie day to day, and should see this. Just ask.

send-ask.text: Send this report to Talha Asif

send-point.text: It found Talha's work email in your staff records. It goes out as a PDF.

crews-lead.text: One page, instead of three reports from three departments. Now pull each thread. Start with the leak nobody reports: crews paid to wait.

crews-ask.text: Where are we paying for crews that aren't producing on Dixie?

crews-point.text: Here it is, in dollars: what we paid crews to stand by, trade by trade.

crews-verify.text: And where those hours were charged, item by item. Nobody hid this. It sat in the site reports. Nobody had time to add it up.

cash-ask.text: How much money is the Dixie & Mayfield job owed right now, and what should we chase first?

cash-point.text: That's what the job is owed right now. The biggest piece is a progress claim the Region has already certified, but not yet paid. Then the extra work waiting on their sign-off.

cash-verify.text: The holdback sits on its own: the Region keeps it until the job is done, so it isn't owed yet. And it tells you what to chase first. Working capital, found with one question.

schedule-lead.text: Now the delays, and which of them belong on a claim.

schedule-ask.text: Which Dixie delays can we bill back to the Region?

schedule-point.text: Every delay on this job, logged by the site, and what each one cost: the change order behind it, approved or still waiting on the Region. An unmarked Bell duct bank. Nesting birds. An archaeological find.

schedule-verify.text: That's the evidence a claim is built on, in dollars. The third-party ones go to the Region; our own rework stays with us.

schedule-map.text: And here's where it's all happening.

dsr-lead.text: Every answer you've just seen is only as good as what comes in from site. So here's the other end: a site supervisor at the end of the day.

dsr-ask.text: I want to fill today's daily site report.

dsr-open.text: The report opens beside the chat. No typing, no dropdowns. Just talking.

fill-1.text: Okay, let's start a daily report. This one's for Dixie Road and Mayfield Road, on the Dixie corridor site. It was a day shift, and the supervisor is Gurpreet Sandhu.

fill-2.text: On item C-15 a today, we had one open-cut foreman, four open-cut labourers and two pipelayers. They each put in ten hours.

fill-3.text: On the same item, we had the 40 tonne excavator going, plus three granular trucks. Those ran ten hours each too.

fill-4.text: And we got three hundred tonnes placed on C-15 a.

fill-5.text: And we lost two hours this morning, waiting on Bell to locate a duct bank at station fourteen plus two-eighty.

fill-5-point.text: Crew, equipment, the quantity against the contract item, and the Bell delay, each matched to the real records. Then one more question.

fill-6-point.text: It says what's left, and goes straight to it.

fill-7.text: Oh right, the weather. It was partly cloudy, twelve degrees.

dsr-review.text: Done. That Bell delay is on the record, at a station, the same day: the paper trail that wins a claim. And these hours feed tomorrow morning's answers.

outro-1.text: So here's what this means for you. Know where a job stands in one minute, not one week. Catch idle crews and unbilled work while it's recoverable. Log every delay the day it happens.

outro-2.text: You don't need more reports. You need fewer steps between the question and the answer. Thank you.
